picks.what: The city and port from the Douro, colored aquatint
picks.why: color general view of the Ribeira waterfront with the cathedral and bishop’s palace on the hill

picks.file: Vedutta della cittá presa dalla Serra do Pilar c1850.jpg
picks.what: The city from the Serra do Pilar, with the suspension bridge, lithograph
picks.why: general view across the Douro; suspension bridge (1843), cathedral and bishop’s palace clear

picks.what: The Douro gorge and the Maria Pia bridge, photograph
picks.why: color view up the Douro along the Porto bank, Eiffel’s Maria Pia bridge in the distance

gaps: P0, P1, P2: nothing (#1 is a 2006 photo dated 1496 by mistake); P6 already covered, not replaced
notes: Also strong but unused: #4 (Frederick William Flower photograph, 1849, one of the earliest photos of the city) — same period as the 1817 aquatint and only months from the about-1850 lithograph; #2 (1833 view during the Siege of Porto, event); #9 (painting dated only ‘19th century’). For P5, #14 (Largo da Ribeira, 1920s postcard) is a landmark street scene but dominated by ox teams. P6: #16 (Ribeira from the Luís I bridge, 2011) and #17 (Diego Delso, 2012) are fine alternatives; I could not compare them with the existing 2013 photo.
